summary: This bill amends 18 U.S.C. 925(a)(1) to extend the federal ban on firearm and ammunition possession by certain aliens to also prohibit government entities from using or providing such weapons to those aliens.

scores.thoughts: The bill makes a narrow amendment to federal firearms statutes regarding who may possess guns while acting for government entities. It contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or cutting any federal expenditures, programs, or appropriations.
The bill does not address tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related provisions.
No provisions relate to health insurance, medical care delivery, public health programs, or market-based healthcare reforms.

The bill expands the reach of existing firearm prohibitions (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(5) and (d)(5)) by removing a statutory exemption previously available to government entities. This imposes an additional restriction on firearm possession, albeit one narrowly targeted at certain non-citizens rather than the general population.

The legislation is explicitly designed to prevent illegal aliens from possessing or using firearms in an official government capacity (e.g., as law-enforcement officers). It therefore strengthens enforcement of immigration-related restrictions on illegal aliens and aligns with efforts to restrict unlawful presence and activity.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions affect military funding, defense procurement, or armed-forces policies.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural-resource management.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or other social safety-net benefits.
The bill makes no changes to education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement appear in the text.
While the bill touches on who may be armed in a law-enforcement capacity, it does not alter sentencing, policing practices, rehabilitation programs, or broader criminal-justice procedures.
The legislation has no bearing on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No fiscal measures, deficit provisions, or debt-related language are present.
The bill does not address legal protections or restrictions related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concern foreign assistance, international aid, or State Department funding.
The bill contains nothing related to voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No data-privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions are included.
The legislation does not address worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
No language addresses religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
